conviction_note: No company-level number the market lacks was found. The evidence is a set of small items pointing both ways: a supportive rate backdrop and benign peer prints, against a stock at an all-time high above the average target, two valuation downgrades, a single-source bar that needs about 4% sequential EPS growth in a seasonally weak deposit quarter, and a record of beats being sold (Q4'25 beat -0.33%, Q1'26 beat -1.97%). So p_up is 47, a small lean down. abs_move_pct is 2.5, above the name's 0.6% median because only three prints exist (two of them beats, both sold) and a scraped implied move of about ±5% looks like an illiquid chain the baseline could not price. impact_sum is -0.1, close to the scaled -0.15, and both are effectively zero.
bar: Q3'26 EPS $0.49, revenue $288.6M, Benzinga consensus page (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CBC/earnings-forecasts, updated about 2026-10-16, read through a search snippet because the page returns 403). There is no company guide and no second agreeing estimate source: the iTiger preview found was for Q1, and Seeking Alpha's figure is a stale full-year number from March. The bar is therefore single-sourced and every finding is capped small. My own run-rate from the Q2 8-K (adjusted EPS $0.47, NII $212.8M, seasonal public-fund outflow in Q3) points to about $0.48, so -1% against the bar.
positioning_check: Short interest, settlement 2026-09-30: 9,097,041 shares, up from 5,953,550 on 09-15 and 5,159,638 on 08-31. That is 3.8% of the 239.5M shares outstanding, with 4.08 days to cover on a late-September average daily volume of 2.23M (equibles.com/stocks/cbc/shortinterest, read 2026-10-26; the 10-15 settlement was not yet published). Free float is thin: only 17.78M shares were sold in the November 2025 IPO and the family holds the rest (walnutinvest/marketchameleon snippet). Float after the May 2026 lock-up expiry is unknown, so short interest as a share of float could be large. The September volume spike suggests index-related hedging (KBW Q3 2026 rebalance, 2026-09-11), but that is not confirmed. Options: the baseline found an empty chain, so there is no skew and no priced lean. Unusual Whales shows a ±4.98% implied move (2026-10-26), which I treat as unreliable given the illiquid chain.

findings.finding: The rate backdrop held up NIM through Q3. The FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% in July (9-3, with three dissents for a hike), and the pre-meeting debate for September was hold versus hike, while the company's own 10-Q assumed 'gradual easing' of prime from 6.75% to 6.25%. That matters because CBC carries 36.2% noninterest-bearing deposits, a back book still repricing (it sold $210M at 2.0% and reinvested at 4.5%) and $7.07B of securities. Its FTE NIM went 4.36% in Q1 to 4.43% in Q2. A Q3 NIM of 4.45% or higher would beat a model built on the company's own easing assumption.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's 7bp NIM expansion came with an EPS print in line with consensus and a +0.63% reaction (baseline, 2026-08-04). This name has not rewarded margin lines strongly.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: sell-side models already carry the rate path, and the stock is up 9.1% in 20 days. If this were unpriced, the consensus would sit at or below Q2's $0.47, but it sits at $0.49, which already embeds some expansion.
findings.independence: Proxy, not company-confirmed. The FOMC July hold and the hold-or-hike framing come from the pre-meeting analysis at https://futuresearch.ai/app/p/a/will-the-u-s-federal-reserve-fomc-announce-a. I did not confirm the September outcome itself.

findings.finding: Missouri and Midwest peers that reported in October were benign, with no credit or deposit scare. Commerce Bancshares (CBSH, Kansas City/St. Louis) reported Q3 EPS of $1.08 against a split consensus of $1.07-1.09. Its underlying NIM, excluding prior-quarter TIPS income, rose to 3.71% from 3.66%, average loans rose $172M and average deposits fell 1.3% on seasonality. Enterprise Financial (St. Louis) held NIM flat at 4.30% and grew deposits $624M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No CBC-specific history on peer read-throughs. The CBSH reaction to its own print was not found.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: both peers reported before CBC's five-day +7.3% run to an all-time high, which is what a priced, benign read-through looks like. The residual is only that the absence of a credit scare is confirmed.
findings.independence: Enterprise Financial Q3 2026 8-K exhibit: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001025835/000102583526000185/ex991financialstatementsan.htm. This is a separate document from the CBSH 8-K, but both are peer proxies.

findings.finding: The bar looks slightly full. Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.47 on NII of $212.8M, a 46.5% efficiency ratio and a $3.5M provision. Management said public-fund deposits would fall seasonally again in Q3 (they had fallen 12.1% QoQ in Q2) and would recover only in Q4. A Q3 run-rate built from the Q2 8-K comes to about $0.48, against a $0.49 consensus that needs about 4% sequential EPS growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 printed $0.47 against a $0.47-0.48 consensus (sources differ) and the stock moved +0.63%. The two earlier prints were beats and were sold (-0.33% and -1.97%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is my inference from a single-source bar. If the market shared it, the stock would not be at an all-time high above the average target. Capped small because the bar is not corroborated.
findings.independence: The seasonal public-fund guidance appears in the Q2 investor deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002065601/000162828026052174/investordeckq22026final.htm) and the Quartr call summary (https://quartr.com/events/central-bancompany-inc-cbc-q2-2026_FR9tgubB). Both are company-derived, so this is one fact.

findings.finding: Valuation sits ahead of the sell side going into the print. Spot is $34.76, at the 52-week high (+65% from the $21 IPO), above the five-analyst average target of $34.60. Stephens (late August) and Morgan Stanley (mid-September) both cut to Equal Weight after Q2. Of the two prior beats, Q4'25 traded -0.33% and Q1'26 traded -1.97%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two beats were sold (2026-01-27 -0.33%, 2026-04-28 -1.97%) and an in-line print rose 0.63% (baseline). Only three prints exist.
findings.why_not_priced: The downgrades are public, but the stock rallied 7.3% in the five days before the print anyway. A fully priced valuation concern would show up as a stock trading below targets, not above them.
findings.independence: The beat history comes from the baseline plus the itiger Q1 preview (https://www.itiger.com/news/1169651858, 2026-04-28), which confirms Q4'25 was a 4% EPS beat. Shrunk for the crowded-short risk noted in positioning_check.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 53% in the second half of September, to 9.10M shares from 5.95M (3.8% of shares outstanding, 4.1 days to cover), against a public float that was only 17.8M shares at the IPO. Against true float the short is plausibly large, which gives a squeeze path if the print is clean.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. Short interest was 4.6-5.2M through the prior print (2026-08-04), with no visible squeeze.
findings.why_not_priced: If the shorts were directional, the five-day +7.3% may already be covering. The rise coincides with a volume spike that looks like index hedging (KBW rebalance), so it may not be directional at all. Small and wide.
findings.independence: The float figure comes from a walnutinvest/marketchameleon search snippet (https://walnutinvest.com/stocks/cbc/is-it-a-buy-or-sell). The KBW Q3 2026 rebalance headline on stockanalysis is unconfirmed as to CBC.

findings.finding: CBC holds $1.9B of capital above its 13.5% CET1 target (consolidated CET1 28.6%) and a fresh $100M buyback (only $7.6M was used in Q2, at $27.13). The CEO is on record hunting about $2B banks, including in Texas. A deal or a bigger buyback could arrive with the print, but nothing is announced and the sign of a deal is ambiguous for the acquirer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The new $100M authorization arrived with Q2 and the stock moved +0.63%.
findings.why_not_priced: The excess capital is fully public. What is unpriced is only whether a deployment arrives at this print, and there is no evidence that it does, so it is sized 0 with a wide band.
findings.independence: S&P Global, January 2026, on the M&A hunt: https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/articles/2026/1/central-bancompany-still-on-the-hunt-for-m-a-target-97559219

findings.finding: Credit is drifting. Nonperforming loans rose to 0.49% of loans HFI from 0.40% at year-end 2025 (0.42% a year ago), nonperforming commercial loans rose 23% QoQ in Q2, and nonaccrual loans were $55.1M against $46.4M a year earlier. Net charge-offs are still only 10bp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 NPL rise printed with a +0.63% reaction, so it has not been punished so far.
findings.why_not_priced: The trend is public, but a stock at an all-time high with two benign peer prints is not pricing a further step-up. If it were, the stock would be lagging KRE, not leading it.
findings.independence: The 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002065601/000162828026057081/cbci-20260630.htm) repeats the same figures. That is one company dataset, so this is one finding.

baseline_tension: There is no option skew to agree or disagree with. The +7.3% five-day and +9.1% twenty-day run to an all-time high cuts slightly against a positive read, and the small negative lean agrees with the run-up being exhausted. It is not strong enough to fight a possibly crowded short on a thin float, so p_up stays close to 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short): the valuation/positioning negative went from -0.4 to -0.3, because short interest rose to 9.1M against a thin float and a squeeze is a mechanism of its own
Rule 6 (single-source bar): confirmed that every finding is already capped at 0.3 or below in absolute size; no change needed
Rule 1 (beats sold): already reflected in p_up 47 and the valuation finding; not applied a second time
Everything else was left standing: the proxies stay filed small (rule 5), and the M&A item stays at 0 with a wide band (rule 3)
